name: Safar
intro:
In the month of Safar, the weight of events lies heavy on the shoulders. The continued mourning for Imam Husayn (AS) on the one hand; the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW), Imam Mujtaba and Imam Reza (AS) on the other; and the beginning of the usurpation of the caliphate on yet another — these are successive tragedies for which we must be in mourning during this month. Events took place on days 1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 19, 20, 24, 26, 27, 28, 29 and 30 of this month, which can be broadly grouped as follows:
Events related to Karbala, which begin with the bringing of the sacred head of Imam Husayn (AS) into Sham (Damascus). Following that came the entry of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) into Sham and then the assembly of Yazid. The martyrdom of Lady Ruqayya (AS) also occurred in the wake of these events. The release of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) from the prison of Sham, their return from Sham to Karbala, Jabir's arrival on Arbaeen to visit Sayyid al-Shuhada (AS), and the reunion of the sacred head of Imam Husayn (AS) with his sacred body in Karbala are the later events.
The tragedies of the other Infallibles begin with the illness of the Messenger of God (SAWW). His martyrdom and the beginning of the tragedies of Lady Zahra (AS) are the first stage. The martyrdom of Imam Mujtaba (AS) and Imam Reza (AS) are the later tragedies.
The death of Salman (RA), the martyrdom of Ammar Yasir, the martyrdom of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, and the martyrdom of Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) are other events that took place in this month.
Alongside these tragedies, the birth of Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) is happy news that brings joy to the friends of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) in this month.
The Prophet's (SAW) request for a shoulder blade (to write on) and the dispatch of Usama's army are among the events of the last year of the Prophet's (SAWW) life. The beginning of the Imamate of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), which was in fact the beginning of the usurpation of his caliphate, follows those bitter days. The start of the Battle of Siffin, Laylat al-Harir at the end of the Siffin war, the matter of the two arbitrators, and then the Battle of Nahrawan are pages from the era of the caliphate of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS).

events.title: Bringing the Sacred Head of Imam Husayn (AS) into Sham
events.text: The Umayyads declared this day a festival because of the entry of the sacred head of Imam Husayn (AS) into Sham.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Muharram & Safar, p. 341. Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. Safar, p. 5. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 596. Taqwim al-Muhsinin: p. 15.

events.title: Entry of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) into Sham
events.text:
When news arrived that the captives of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) were approaching Damascus, Yazid issued orders:
1. A jewel-studded crown and a throne inlaid with precious stones were to be prepared.
2. The notables of each guild were to work together to adorn the city in the utmost splendor.
3. All the people of the city were to wear festive clothes and adorn themselves.
4. Everyone was to go about the streets and congratulate one another.
5. Once fully ready, they were to go out with drums and trumpets to welcome the captives.
6. Criers were to proclaim in the city: The severed heads and the women and children of those who set out for Iraq with the aim of overthrowing the government are entering the city, but the Caliph's agent, Ibn Ziyad, has killed them. Whoever loves the Caliph should rejoice today.
The vile Syrians, for their part, did not fall short: they raised colorful banners over the rooftops and spread out wine at every crossing. The songs of singers rose, and the people went in groups toward the Kufa Gate of Damascus, while some had left the city. This was while the grieving, bereaved family of the Prophet (SAWW) — whose sacred precinct had Gabriel the Trustworthy as its guardian — was brought through the Sa'at Gate by merciless spear-bearers with whips in their hands. As soon as those vile fools saw the luminous company of captives, they began to speak insolently. What happened in that city and what they did to those noble ones — the pen has no strength to write it.
sources: Ma'ali al-Sibtayn: vol. 2, p. 140. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 6, p. 294.

Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 5, pp. 6 - 30. Az Madinah ta Madinah (From Medina to Medina): pp. 896 - 899. Also adapted from Nasikh al-Tawarikh, 'Awalim al-'Ulum, Muhayyij al-Ahzan, Riyad al-Masa'ib, Al-Luhuf, Amali of Sheikh Saduq, and Al-Dam'a al-Sakiba.

events.title: Start of the Battle of Siffin
events.text:
After the letters and admonitions of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) to Mu'awiya in the month of Muharram proved fruitless, on Wednesday, the first of Safar, 38 AH, the army of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) drew up in line facing the army of Sham. The Imam's army numbered 90,000 and Mu'awiya's army 85,000.
The army of disbelief cut off the water from the army of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), but after Imam Husayn (AS) seized the water and reopened it, the Imam's army did not prevent the water from reaching Mu'awiya's army.
After a number of his companions were martyred, the Imam suddenly attacked Mu'awiya's army with ten thousand men of the tribe of Rabi'a, broke their ranks, and reached Mu'awiya's tent. He said: O Mu'awiya, why do you send people to their deaths? Come and fight me, so that whichever of us is killed, the caliphate will belong to the other!
Amr ibn al-As said to Mu'awiya: Ali has spoken to you fairly. Mu'awiya said: But you were not fair in this counsel, for whoever goes out to face him does not return safely! It was at this point that Mu'awiya forced Amr ibn al-As to go out and fight the Imam. As soon as the Imam recognized him, he raised his sword to send him to Hell, but Amr ibn al-As resorted to a trick and exposed his private parts. The Imam turned his face away from that shameless man, and that wretch fled. Finally, by trickery, they put several pages of the Quran on spear-tips, and the affair of the two arbitrators arose.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Muharram & Safar, p. 339. Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 5. Tatimmat al-Muntaha: pp. 24 - 29. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 176.
Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 23.

events.title: The Assembly of Yazid
events.text: According to one account, on this day the captives of the Family of the Messenger were brought into the assembly of Yazid. It is worth reflecting: who were brought in, in what condition, and into what kind of assembly?
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Muharram & Safar, p. 353.

events.title: Martyrdom of Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS)
events.text: In the year 121 AH, Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) was martyred in Kufa. His uprising had been on the first of Muharram. After he was buried, on this day or on 19 Rabi' al-Awwal, they dug up his grave, removed the body of that noble man from the grave, dragged it along the ground, and hanged it.
sources: Al-Irshad: vol. 2, p. 174. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 596.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Muharram & Safar, p. 15.
Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 4, p. 67

events.title: Martyrdom of Lady Ruqayya (AS)
events.text:
On the fifth day of the month of Safar, 61 AH, Lady Ruqayya was martyred in oppression. Her noble names are “Ruqayya,” “Fatima,” and “Zaynab.” Her father was Mawlana, the Martyr Aba Abdillah al-Husayn (AS), and her mother was Umm Ishaq. She was born in Medina, and at the age of three or more she came to Karbala with her noble father in Muharram 61 AH. Before and after the day of Ashura she was repeatedly shown care and consolation by Aba Abdillah (AS), to the point that he gave instructions concerning her to his sister Lady Zaynab (AS). After the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (AS), the Ahl al-Bayt and the companions, she was taken with the captives to Kufa and Sham, and on the forty-stage journey to Sham she suffered many hardships. In Sham, after seeing the luminous head of her father with its broken forehead in the ruins, she wept and lamented until she joined the highest heavenly realm, and her noble body was buried at night.
Among the oldest sources in which her name is mentioned with the word Ruqayya is the ode of Sayf ibn 'Umayra al-Nakha'i al-Kufi, one of the companions of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq and Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS):
و عبدکم سیف فتی ابن عمیره عبد لعبد عبید حیدر قنبر
و سکینه عنها السکینه فارقت لما ابتدیت بفرقه و تغیر
و رقیه رق الحسود لضعفها و غدا لیعذرها الذی لم یعذر
و لام کلثوم یجد جدیدها لثم عقیب دموعها لم یکرر
لم أنسها و سکینه و رقیه یبکینه بتحسر و تزفر
(The verses above are in Arabic in the original and are kept as they are.)
There is abundant evidence and documentation concerning the noble existence of this Lady and the presence of her grave at the current location of the sacred shrine, together with miracles and wonders from that oppressed Lady; some of these are referred to in the footnote.
sources: Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 5, pp. 70, 74, 75, 81. Az Madinah ta Madinah: pp. 963 - 965.

Encyclopedia of Shi'ism: vol. 8, pp. 313 - 314. Kamil-e Baha'i: vol. 2, p. 179. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 388. Al-Islamic Shi'i Encyclopedia: vol. 1, part 2, p. 25. Kitab al-Minan (Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ahmad al-Sha'rani, Shafi'i, Egyptian), d. 973 AH.

Nafas al-Mahmum: p. 414. Kitab al-Minan (Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ahmad al-Sha'rani, Shafi'i, Egyptian), d. 973 AH. Ma'ali al-Sibtayn: vol. 2, p. 170. Al-Luhuf of Sayyid Ibn Tawus. Ihqaq al-Haqq: vol. 11, p. 633. Mabki al-'Uyun. The Shining Star of Sham: p. 16. The Heart-Rending Story of Lady Ruqayya (AS): p. 27. Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 3, p. 192. Lady Ruqayya (AS), Herald of Karbala. Elegy of the Family of Muhammad (AS): p. 34. Thamarat al-Hayat: vol. 2, p. 38. Mukhtasar Tarikh Dimashq: vol. 9, p. 174. Bahr al-Gharaib: vol. 2. events.title: Martyrdom of Imam Mujtaba (AS)
events.text: According to one account, on this day in the year 49 AH, Imam Mujtaba (AS) was martyred in Medina at the age of 47. However, the more widely held view among the Imami scholars is that his martyrdom was at the end of the month of Safar.
sources: Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 6. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 598.
Jala' al-'Uyun: vol. 270. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 184. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44, p. 134.

events.title: Birth of Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (AS)
events.text:
According to the well-known view, on this day (a Sunday) in the year 128 AH, in “Abwa'” between Mecca and Medina, Hazrat Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) was born. His exalted father was Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and his mother was Hamida al-Musaffat (AS).
The most famous titles of the Imam are Salih, Sabir, Amin and Kazim, and his most famous kunya is Abu al-Hasan. Although Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) and Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) also bear this kunya, in the books of hadith Imam al-Kazim (AS) is referred to as Abu al-Hasan the First, Imam Reza (AS) as Abu al-Hasan the Second, and Hazrat al-Hadi (AS) as Abu al-Hasan the Third. Sometimes, because of taqiyya, he has also been referred to as the Righteous Servant, the jurist, and the scholar.
sources: I'lam al-Wara: vol. 2, p. 6. Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 6. Manaqib Ibn Shahrashub: vol. 4, p. 349. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 596. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 48, p. 9. Jala' al-'Uyun: p. 524. Al-Kafi: vol. 3, p. 507.
Rayahin al-Shari'a: vol. 3, p. 18. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 48, pp. 1 - 6.
Jala' al-'Uyun: p. 524. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 516. Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 2, p. 181.

events.title: Death of Salman (RA)
events.text:
Salman (RA) passed away in Mada'in in the year 36 AH at the age of 250 — according to one account, 350. He has been given the titles Salman ibn al-Islam, Salman the Pure, and Salman Muhammadi, and he is addressed with the words: Peace be upon you, O one who mingled his faith with the pure Ahl al-Bayt.
Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) said: “Salman was among those who prayed over Lady Zahra (AS).”
Imam al-Sadiq (AS) also said: “Salman comprehended the first and the last knowledge; he is an ocean of which not everyone has a share, and he belongs to the Ahl al-Bayt.”
His biography has been narrated in various books, and as for the greatness of his rank and worth, it is enough that Mawlana Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) brought the means of washing and shrouding him, washed and shrouded him, prayed over him, and buried him.
Gabriel said to the Prophet (SAWW): “Paradise's longing for Salman is greater than his longing for Paradise.”
sources: Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 1, p. 355.
Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. Safar, p. 270. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 6, p. 294.
Salman ibn al-Islam: p. 1.
Part of the ziyara of Salman (RA). Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 99, p. 289. Nafas al-Rahman fi Fada'il Salman: p. 640.
Al-Ikhtisas: p. 4.
Al-Ikhtisas: p. 8.
Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 5, p. 325.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 18, p. 135.

events.title: Martyrdom of Ammar and Khuzayma
events.text:
On this day in the year 37 AH, Ammar Yasir, at the age of 93, and Khuzayma ibn Thabit were martyred in the Battle of Siffin.
Ammar's father was Yasir ibn Amir, who was the first man in Islam to be martyred at the hands of the polytheists in Mecca. Ammar's mother was Sumayya, who endured the torment of the disbelievers of Mecca with great patience and was the first woman martyr in Islam, martyred at the hands of Abu Jahl.
Ammar was killed by Abu al-'Adiya and Abu Hawa' al-Saksaki. When the news reached Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), he was deeply grieved. He came to Ammar's bedside, placed his head on his knee, and with great sorrow and grief recited verses about the faithlessness of the world and separation from loved ones. Then he said: “Indeed we belong to God, and to Him we shall return. Whoever is not saddened by the killing of Ammar has no share in being a Muslim. Paradise has become obligatory for Ammar not once but many times.”
sources: Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 16. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 189. Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 2, p. 100.
Tatimmat al-Muntaha: pp. 26, 27

events.title: Battle of Nahrawan
events.text: On the ninth of Safar, 39 AH, the conquest of Nahrawan took place, and Dhu al-Thudayya, the leader of the Kharijites, was sent to Hell.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 56, p. 138. Manaqib Ibn Shahrashub: vol. 3, p. 220.

events.title: Laylat al-Harir in the Battle of Siffin
events.text:
The final engagement of the Siffin war was the battle of “Laylat al-Harir,” on the night of Friday, the eleventh of Safar, 38 AH. On that night Mu'awiya's troops howled like dogs from the intensity of the cold, because “harir” is the word for the sound of dogs.
Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), with Dhu al-Fiqar in hand and mounted on the horse of the Prophet (SAWW), struck with the sword; with every blow he said “Allahu Akbar” and brought a brave warrior down to the dust. The number of those slain by his hand that night is reported at more than 500, and they fought until morning, so much so that Dhu al-Fiqar was bent several times and that noble one straightened it with his blessed knee.
In this battle a number of the army of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) were martyred, among them Ammar Yasir, Uways al-Qarani, Hashim al-Mirqal, Hashim's son Khuzayma ibn Thabit, Safwan ibn Hudhayfa, Abdullah ibn Budayl with his brother Abd al-Rahman ibn Budayl, and Abdullah ibn al-Harith, the brother of Malik al-Ashtar, who were among the close companions of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS). A great number of Mu'awiya's army were sent to Hell, and this war lasted 14 months. In the end, through the trickery of Amr ibn al-As and the hypocrisy of some such as Ash'ath ibn Qays al-Kindi, matters ended in arbitration.
sources: Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: pp. 163 - 164.

events.title: The Two Arbitrators at Siffin
events.text:
On the morning of the twelfth or thirteenth of Safar, 38 AH, the army of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) was getting ready for battle, but Amr ibn al-As resorted to a trick and ordered that the Qurans be raised on spears. In the front ranks of the army of disbelief were pages of the Quran, and in the other ranks everyone raised whatever he had on a spear!! And they cried out: There is no judgment but God's! The hypocrites such as Ash'ath ibn Qays, by weakening the morale of the Imam's army, encouraged them to accept the two arbitrators. However much Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) said that this was a ruse and that he was the Speaking Book of God, it had no effect. Finally it was agreed that each army would appoint an arbitrator on its own behalf, and that both sides would accept their ruling.
Mu'awiya put forward Amr ibn al-As, and Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) said: “If we have no choice, let it be Abdullah ibn Abbas, otherwise Malik al-Ashtar al-Nakha'i.”
Ash'ath and the group of Quran reciters and memorizers, who later became part of the Kharijites, were satisfied with neither of the two and said: “Only Abdullah ibn Qays, that is, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.” The hypocrisy of the hypocrites succeeded, and Abu Musa and Amr ibn al-As met at “Dumat al-Jandal” — a fortress between Medina and Sham — and, given the enmity that both of them bore toward the Banu Hashim, especially Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), and through the scheming and trickery of Amr ibn al-As, they apparently deposed the Imam. Abu Musa was among the hypocrites who, on the Night of 'Aqaba (after Ghadir), intended to kill the Prophet (SAWW).
Thus on the following day, in front of the crowd, Abu Musa said to Amr: You stand and depose Mu'awiya from the leadership, so that I may depose Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS). Amr ibn al-As said: I will never get ahead of you, who were a governor of Abu Bakr and Umar and who preceded me in faith and in the Hijra! Ibn Abbas said: Abu Musa! Do not let the son of Nabigha deceive you; but he did not heed Ibn Abbas's words, stood up, took the ring off his hand and said: I have deposed Ali and Mu'awiya from the caliphate, and fell silent.
The accursed Amr ibn al-As stood up and said: “People, you heard that Abu Musa deposed Ali from the caliphate. I too depose him from the caliphate, and I confirm it for Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, for he is more deserving, and as a sign of appointing Mu'awiya I put the ring on my hand!”
To deceive the public, the two arbitrators hurled many curses and insults at each other and grabbed each other by the collar, and Shurayh the judge struck Amr ibn al-As on the head with a whip. Out of fear of the companions of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), Abu Musa took refuge in Mecca. All of this happened even though the Prophet (SAWW), during the expedition of Dumat al-Jandal, had informed Abu Musa of this affair and said: “The two arbitrators at Dumat al-Jandal are misguided, and they will mislead those who follow them.”
After this event, Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) would curse Abu Musa and three others in the qunut of his voluntary prayers in this manner: O God, curse Mu'awiya, Amr, Abu al-A'war al-Sulami, and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Muharram & Safar, p. 385.
Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 6, p. 294.
Sharh Ibn Abi al-Hadid: vol. 13, pp. 314, 315.
Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 167. Tatimmat al-Muntaha: pp. 30 - 31. Sharh Ibn Abi al-Hadid: vol. 13, p. 315.
Sharh Ibn Abi al-Hadid: vol. 13, p. 315.

events.title: Martyrdom of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr
events.text:
On this day in the year 38 AH, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, at the age of 28, was martyred by poison on the orders of Mu'awiya and Amr ibn al-As; according to one account, this was in mid-Jumada al-Thani.
After his martyrdom, they placed him inside the belly of a dead donkey and burned him. The grave attributed to him holds what remained of that noble man's burned body. When the enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) go to that noble man's grave, they turn their backs to the grave and recite the Fatiha for Abu Bakr!?
sources: Fayd al-'Allam: p. 249. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 733.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Muharram & Safar, p. 395. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 6, p. 294.

events.title: Beginning of the Prophet's (SAW) Illness
events.text: The illness of the Prophet (SAWW), which led to his passing, began in the middle of the month of Safar.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 31, p. 633; vol. 37, p. 116.

events.title: Arbaeen of Sayyid al-Shuhada (AS)
events.text: On such a day, forty days have passed since the grievous tragedy of the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (AS), the Ahl al-Bayt, and his faithful companions. It is incumbent upon the friends and Shi'a of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) to honor this day by wearing black, suspending work, holding mourning gatherings, taking part in chest-beating gatherings, and recounting the tragedy.

events.title: Jabir's Pilgrimage to Karbala
events.text: On this day in the year 61 AH, Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari and his companions, about forty days after the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (AS), arrived in Karbala from Medina. Together with 'Atiyya, he visited the grave of his beloved, Sayyid al-Shuhada (AS).
sources: Tawdih al-Maqasid: pp. 6 - 7.

events.title: Return of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) to Karbala
events.text: According to the well-known view, on such a day the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) returned from Sham to Karbala.
sources: Masar al-Shi'a: p. 26. Al-'Udad al-Qawiyya: p. 219. Wasa'il al-Shi'a: vol. 14, p. 478. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 730. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 328. Ma'ali al-Sibtayn: vol. 2, p. 191. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 195. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 97, p. 329. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 596.

events.title: Reunion of the Sacred Head of Imam Husayn (AS) with the Sacred Body
events.text: On this day — according to the view of Sayyid Murtada — the noble head of Imam Husayn (AS) was brought from Sham to Karbala by Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) and was joined to his sacred body.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44, p. 199.

events.title: The Prophet's (SAW) Request for a Shoulder Blade
events.text:
On this day the Prophet (SAWW) asked for an inkwell and a shoulder blade so that he could write that the immediate caliphate belongs to Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), but Umar prevented this, insolently offended the sacred person of the Prophet (SAWW), and said: Inna al-rajula layahjur: “This man is raving!”
Also on this day the Prophet (SAWW) ascended the pulpit, delivered a sermon, admonished the people, and called them to follow the Quran and the Itra (his Family).
sources: Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 6, p. 2 ).5 Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 22, p. 473.

events.title: Dispatch of Usama's Army
events.text: On this day in the year 11 AH, the Prophet (SAWW) ordered a select group of the companions, and especially Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman, to prepare for a journey to Rome and war with the Romans under the command of Usama ibn Zayd. They were reluctant about this order and objected to Usama's command over the army of Islam to the Seal of the Prophets (SAWW). The Prophet said: “May God curse whoever lags behind the army of Usama,” but even so, Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman lagged behind and returned!
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 30, p. 428; vol. 21, p. 410. Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd: vol. 2, p. 136. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 6, p. 295.

events.title: Martyrdom of the Messenger of God (SAW)
events.text: The heart-rending and oppressed martyrdom of the noblest of creation, the Seal of the Prophets, Muhammad ibn Abdullah (SAW), in the year 11 AH at the age of 63, was by poison; and according to some narrations, Aisha and Hafsa poisoned him! On 24 Safar the Prophet's (SAWW) illness grew severe. During his illness the Prophet (SAWW) said: Bring my beloved to me. Aisha and Hafsa brought their fathers to him. The Prophet (SAWW) turned his blessed face away from them and said: “Bring my beloved to me.” Then they sent for Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS). When his blessed gaze fell upon him, he called him close and spoke some words to him. When Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) left his presence, Umar and Abu Bakr said to him: “What did your friend tell you?” He replied: “He narrated to me a thousand chapters of knowledge, from each of which a thousand other chapters open.”
sources: I'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 80. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 17, p. 406. Ithbat al-Hudat: vol. 1, p. 604. Al-Kharaij wa al-Jara'ih: vol. 1, p. 27. Basa'ir al-Darajat: p. 503. Al-Mahasin of al-Barqi: vol. 2, p. 262. Jami' al-Usul: vol. 11, p. 38. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 6, p. 295. Al-Tabaqat al-Kubra: vol. 2, p. 154. Sunan Abi Dawud: vol. 4, p. 174.
Tafsir al-Safi: vol. 1, p. 389.
Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 6, p. 295.
Al-Kafi: vol. 2, p. 61. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 22, p. 473.

subsections.title: Bequests of the Prophet (SAW)
subsections.text:
In the last moments of his life, the Prophet (SAWW) gave bequests to Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), and took Gabriel, Michael, and the angels nearest to God as witnesses to that bequest. Among the words that Gabriel was saying to the Prophet (SAWW) and Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) was hearing was this: “They will usurp your [khamast — unclear in the Persian source], they will tear the veil of your sanctity, and your beard will be dyed with the blood of your head.”
Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) said: “When I understood those words, I cried out and fell upon the ground.” Then he spoke words to Lady Zahra (AS) and to al-Hasanayn, Hasan and Husayn (AS). Then that testament was sealed with several golden seals which fire had not touched (and which were not made by human hands) and was handed over to Amir al-Mu'minin (AS).
sources: Al-Kafi: vol. 2, pp. 32 - 33.

subsections.title: Washing and Praying over the Body of the Prophet (SAW)
subsections.text: After washing the Prophet's body, Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) prayed over him alone. The people, except for the companions of the Saqifa, had gathered in the mosque and were thinking about the prayer over the Prophet (SAWW) and his burial. Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) came and said: “The Messenger of God (SAWW) is our Imam in his life and after his passing” — an indication that the prayer over his noble body would not be performed in congregation. At this point the people entered in groups and, without an imam, recited three times the verse “Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, ask [Allah to confer] blessing upon him and ask [Allah to grant him] peace,” and then came out.
sources: Al-Irshad: vol. 1, pp. 188 - 189.
Surah Al-Ahzab: verse 56.

subsections.title: Burial of the Blessed Body of the Prophet (SAW)
subsections.text: Then Mawla al-Muwahhidin (AS) said: In whatever place God takes the soul of His Prophet, He is pleased that he be buried in that very place, and I shall bury him in the chamber in which he passed away. Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), with the help of others, dug a grave and placed the Prophet's body in it. Then he himself went down into the grave, uncovered the face of the Prophet (SAWW), laid the right cheek on the ground, and they closed the niche and poured earth over it.
sources: Al-Irshad: vol. 1, pp. 188 - 189.

subsections.title: A Summary of the Life of the Prophet (SAW)
subsections.text:
He was two months old — and according to one account still in the womb — when his noble father Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib (AS) passed away. He was 4, or 7, or 8 years old when his mother Amina bint Wahb passed away in Abwa'. Eight years, two months and ten days of his noble life had passed when his noble grandfather Abd al-Muttalib (AS) passed away. At the age of 25 he married Lady Khadija al-Kubra (AS), who was 40 years old.
Thirty years of his blessed life had passed when Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) was born. At 40 God sent him as a prophet. At 45 he ascended on the Mi'raj, and in the fifth year of the mission Lady Fatima Zahra (AS) was born.
Fifty years of his blessed life had passed when Abu Talib and Khadija al-Kubra (AS) passed away. At 45 he ascended on the Mi'raj. Fifty-two years, eleven months and thirteen days of his blessed life had passed when he migrated to Medina the Illuminated. After the Hijra he was honored with a stay of roughly ten years in Medina, until on 28 Safar of the year 11 AH he passed away, poisoned.
At the time of the Prophet's (SAWW) passing, Lady Zahra (AS) was weeping greatly. The Prophet called her to him and said something that calmed Fatima's (AS) sorrow and grief. When she was asked the reason, she said: “My father informed me that I would be the first of his household to join him, and that the duration of this separation would not be long.”
sources: Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: pp. 36 to 46.
Al-Irshad: vol. 1, p. 187.

events.title: Beginning of the Imamate of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS)
events.text: This is the first day of the Imamate of Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS), and visiting him (ziyara) on this day is recommended.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 97, p. 384.

events.title: Beginning of the Usurpation of the Caliphate
events.text: This is the first day of the unjust usurpation of the caliphate, the confining of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) to his house, and the breaking of the pledge of Ghadir Day by the people of the Saqifa of Banu Sa'ida.
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 9.

events.title: Martyrdom of Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (AS)
events.text:
On this day in the year 50 AH, Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (AS) was martyred. According to one account his martyrdom occurred on 7 Safar, and according to another on 5 Rabi' al-Awwal.
Ja'da, the daughter of Ash'ath ibn Qays, poisoned him with the poison that Mu'awiya had sent her. Along with the poison Mu'awiya sent a hundred thousand dirhams and promised that he would marry her to Yazid; but he did not keep his promise.
sources: I'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 403. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 95, p. 200. Masar al-Shi'a: p. 27. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 199. Al-Kafi: vol. 1, p. 461. Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 1, p. 231. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 6, p. 295. Al-'Udad al-Qawiyya: p. 350.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44, p. 161.
Al-Irshad: vol. 2, p. 16. Al-Kafi: vol. 2, p. 481. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44, p. 149. Tarikh al-Khulafa: p. 192.

subsections.title: The Poisoning of the Imam
subsections.text: The poisoning of Imam Hasan (AS) lasted forty days. After the effects of the poison appeared on his blessed body and the time of martyrdom drew near, he said to Sayyid al-Shuhada (AS): “I have been poisoned, and pieces of my liver are in the basin. I am parting from you and joining God, and I know who poisoned me; but by the right I have over you, do not say a word about it. When I have passed away, close my eyes, wash me, shroud me, and take me to the side of the grave of my grandfather the Prophet (SAWW) so that I may renew my covenant with him. Then bury me in Baqi' beside my grandmother Fatima bint Asad (AS). I know that the opponents and the hostile will think that you want to bury me beside the Prophet (SAWW), and they will prevent you. I adjure you by God that, because of me, not even a cupping-measure of blood be shed.” Then the Imam gave a testament to his children and household like what Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) had bequeathed, and passed away.
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 41.

subsections.title: The Funeral Procession of the Imam
subsections.text:
After the washing, shrouding and prayer, Imam Husayn (AS) carried him toward the noble resting place of the Prophet (SAWW). On seeing this scene, no doubt remained for Marwan and the rest of the Umayyads, who had come armed and accompanied by Aisha, that he intended to bury him beside the Prophet (SAWW).
So they came and obstructed, and Aisha, while riding a mule, said: “What business do I have with you, that you want to bury in my house someone I do not love?” The accursed Marwan said similar things, and Ibn Abbas replied to him and to Aisha. The sons of Uthman also obstructed and said: “It will never be that Uthman is buried in the worst of places while Hasan is laid to rest beside the Messenger of God.”
Imam Husayn (AS) said: By the God who made Mecca and the Sanctuary sacred, Hasan (AS), the son of Ali and Fatima (AS), is more deserving of the Prophet (SAWW) than those who entered his house without permission. By God, he is more deserving than the bearer of Uthman's faults, who expelled Abu Dharr from Medina, and... Aisha went before the grave of the Prophet (SAWW) and said: “As long as a single hair remains on my head, I will not let you bury him here!” At this the Banu Marwan showered his bier with arrows. The Banu Hashim reached for their swords, but Imam Husayn (AS) prevented them and said: “My brother's testament must not be lost,” and then they pulled seven arrows out of his body! And this was while Imam Mujtaba (AS) had informed Imam Husayn (AS) what crime Aisha would commit after his martyrdom.
Afterward Sayyid al-Shuhada (AS) spoke words to the effect that, were it not for my brother's testament, you would have known where and how God's swords would have fallen upon you. Then they brought his sacred body to Baqi' and buried him beside his grandmother Fatima bint Asad (AS).
Hazrat Mujtaba (AS) had 15 children, daughters and sons, but had no children from Ja'da.
sources: Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 1, p. 235.
Majma' al-Bahrayn: vol. 1, p. 454.
Al-Irshad: vol. 2, pp. 17 - 19. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44, p. 156.
Al-Irshad: vol. 2, p. 20.

events.title: Martyrdom of Imam Reza (AS)
events.text: Hazrat Thamin al-Hujaj (the Eighth Proof), Mawlana Ali ibn Musa al-Reza (AS), was martyred in the year 203 AH — according to the soundest view, two years after the death of Lady Ma'suma (AS). The Imam's blessed age was 49 or 55 years. According to one account, Imam Reza (AS) was martyred on 27 Safar, but the well-known view is the end of the month of Safar. On 28 Safar, Ma'mun forced Imam Reza (AS) to eat poisoned grapes or poisoned pomegranate juice.
sources: Al-Kafi: vol. 2, p. 528. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 200. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 49, p. 292. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 6, p. 295. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 578.
Kashf al-Ghumma: vol. 2, p. 267. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 49, p. 292.
Taj al-Mawalid: p. 50.
Al-Irshad: vol. 2, p. 270. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 6, p. 295. Jala' al-'Uyun: p. 551. Muruj al-Dhahab: vol. 4, p. 28. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 49, p. 298.

subsections.title: Ma'mun's Mistreatment of the Imam
subsections.text:
Ma'mun did not hold back from tormenting and insulting the Imam, and even imprisoned him in shackles for three months in Sarakhs.
After the appointment as heir apparent, the beginning of the Imam's afflictions was his association with the hypocritical, accursed Ma'mun. Outwardly he strove to show reverence and respect for the Imam, but inwardly, by tormenting and harassing the Proof of God, he had made himself content with the Imam's death.
sources: Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 580.

subsections.title: The Poisoning of the Imam
subsections.text:
Yasir the servant says: Every Friday when the Imam returned from the congregational mosque, with a sweaty and dusty body, he would raise his hands to the Divine court and say: “O God, if the relief and resolution of my affair lies in my death, then hasten my death.” The Imam was constantly in sorrow and grief until he passed away in a foreign land.
After Ma'mun concealed the matter of the Imam's martyrdom for a day and a night, he sent for Muhammad, the son of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), and a group of the family of Abu Talib so that they could see the soundness of the Imam's body, and after that he began to weep and wail!!
sources: Fayd al-'Allam: p. 99. Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 280. Wasa'il al-Shi'a: vol. 2, p. 659.
Al-Irshad: vol. 2, p. 271.

subsections.title: Burial of the Imam's Blessed Body
subsections.text:
After the washing, shrouding and prayer over the Imam's noble body, which were performed by Imam al-Jawad (AS), they buried him in front of the grave of Harun, in the house of Humayd ibn Qahtaba, the present place of burial. According to some narrations, Ma'mun, fearing public unrest, ordered that the Imam be buried at night.
The duration of his Imamate was 20 years. The noble age of Imam al-Jawad (AS) at the time of the martyrdom of Imam Reza (AS) was 7 years and a few months.
The reported dates of his martyrdom are: 23 Ramadan, 17 Safar, 27 Safar, 14 Safar, 21 Ramadan, and 23 Dhu al-Qa'da. The great Shi'a scholars in various books have stated that the month of martyrdom was Safar and the day mostly the end of Safar, but they have not stated whether Safar had 29 or 30 days in the year of the martyrdom.
sources: Al-Irshad: vol. 2, p. 271. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 99.

honorifics.(SAWW): Sallallahu Alayhi wa Alihi wa Sallam — peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his progeny (the Prophet Muhammad)
honorifics.(PBUH): Peace Be Upon Him (used for Imams, Prophets and other holy figures, male)
honorifics.(SA): Salamullah Alayha — peace be upon her (Lady Fatima, Lady Umm Kulthum, Lady Zaynab, Lady Narjis, etc.)
honorifics.(PBUT): Peace Be Upon Them (plural, e.g. the Ahl al-Bayt / the Infallible Imams)
honorifics.(ATFS): Ajjalallahu Ta'ala Farajahu ash-Sharif — may Allah hasten his noble reappearance (the Imam of the Age)
honorifics.(RA): Rahimahullah — may Allah have mercy on him
